Monthly SEO Reporting: What Should Your Provider Be Measuring?

Know which Search Console measures belong in a useful monthly SEO report and what they cannot tell you alone.

By Cyberfreak Software · 28 November 2026

A report should help you decide what to do

A monthly SEO report should make the data understandable and connect it to decisions. A table of figures without context is difficult to use. Look for a summary of changes, notable patterns, limitations and the next sensible actions.

Clicks and impressions

Google Search Console reports clicks from Google Search and impressions when a result is shown. Reviewing them over a consistent period can reveal whether visibility or visits are changing. Compare similar date ranges and consider seasonality, changes to the site and the search terms involved.

Queries and pages

Query data can show the searches associated with impressions and clicks, while page data shows which URLs appear in results. These views can highlight pages that may need clearer titles, stronger answers or better internal links. They do not show every search, and low-volume data may be limited.

Indexing and sitemap signals

A report may note indexed pages and issues surfaced in Search Console. A submitted sitemap helps communicate the URLs you want search engines to discover, but submission does not guarantee indexing. The provider should identify meaningful issues rather than treating a raw count as a success measure.

Measures beyond Search Console

Search Console does not measure every business outcome. Enquiries, sales, calls and booked appointments need suitable analytics or CRM tracking, configured with appropriate consent and tested carefully. Ask how reporting distinguishes search visibility from actual commercial outcomes.

Ask for interpretation and next steps

The provider should explain what changed, why it may matter, what remains uncertain and who is responsible for acting.
